quote: Relationship between site elevation (cm above mean sea level) and flooding frequency (days per month) for each month of the year. Green colour coding shows elevations that are optimal for planting, and red indicates areas where careful site assessment is needed before deciding to plant. The brighter the red, the greater the need for site assessment. Elevations above 200 cm (2 m) and below mean sea level may be unsuitable for planting mangroves. Flooding frequency (days flooded per month) is based on tidal records from Ganh Hao tide station for the period 2010 to 2013. Note that the flooding frequency refers to the lower end (marked) of each elevation range, and the number of days flooded decreases with increasing elevation within each elevation band.

context.practice_as_described: pre-rehabilitation assessment of degraded mangrove sites
context.vertical_reference: local mean sea level; not an interchangeable global DEM datum

model_use.method: local graphical planting guidance based on tidal records

reported_values.above_200_cm_and_below_MSL: may be unsuitable, not absolute exclusions
reported_values.frequency: days flooded per month at lower end of elevation band
reported_values.graph: green optimum/red assessment warning; continuous colour transition does not specify exact optimum endpoints

context.numeric_calibration: No response scores, hard endpoints, global elevation envelope or executable function. Retain original cm above local MSL. Tidal frequency is not percent time flooded.
context.applicability_hold: Only degraded mangrove rehabilitation in Bac Lieu; no authorization to convert naturally unvegetated intertidal habitat. Source p41 warns river-mouth station tides differ from exposed coast and estimates lack independent verification. Site modification, rainfall, drainage and species choice qualify guidance.
context.review_needed: Does the local directional guidance apply to this rehabilitation site and datum? Approval must not create global cutoffs.
context.note: Graph visually checked with caption. Source guidance, not validated field response curve; no human approval.
